notes.title: We're part of WDC World Ocean Day Charity Sale! | 75% off SILT
notes.notes:
We are excited to announce that we are supporting [b]WDC[/b],[b] Whale and Dolphin Conservation[/b] for [b]World Ocean Day[/b]!   

The WDC World Ocean Day Sale starts right now and runs until 12th June, 10am PDT 2025, and you can save a fin-tastic 75% off [b]SILT[/b].

[h2]Who are WDC?[/h2]
WDC, Whale and Dolphin Conservation are the leading global charity dedicated to the protection of whales and dolphins. 
Their expert-led teams in the UK, Europe, the Americas, and Australasia work across the whole spectrum of threats, from climate breakdown to accidental entanglements in fishing gear, pollution, captivity and hunting and whaling. They bring together, and work hand-in-hand with, businesses, philanthropists, scientists, NGOs, governments and grassroots communities to find solutions to the problems faced by whales and dolphins.
Their mission is to reverse the global decline of whale and dolphin populations by creating safe seas for these majestic beings. And their vision is a world where every whale and dolphin is safe and free.

[h2]What is ghost gear?[/h2]
Ghost gear is fishing gear that has been lost or abandoned at sea. It’s a deadly menace to whales, dolphins and other marine life. 
When a whale or dolphin gets tangled in it, it can kill them in the most horrific way, by preventing them from getting to the surface to breathe. Or they can carry it for days, weeks or even months suffering a slow and painful death as it cuts into their skin, restricts their movement and hampers their ability to hunt and feed. 
But it’s difficult and expensive for fishers and other ocean users to dispose of gear they find at sea, or even to responsibly get rid of their own gear at the end of its life.
Did you know that about 1/3 of marine litter found in European seas is discarded fishing gear? That's estimated to be over 11,000 tonnes entering the sea each year!
It is a massive problem and so WDC are working on some innovative solutions.  

[h2]How your support will help this year[/h2]
By purchasing SILT and other games from this year’s World Ocean Day sale, you will help WDC continue their global conservation work, as well as their ghost gear removal project, funding 10 missions for divers to remove lethal entanglement hazards to marine life (and scuba divers) from reefs, seabed and shipwrecks in UK seas.

Whales and dolphins are awe-inspiring, intelligent beings. The ocean produces more oxygen and absorbs more carbon than all of Earth's forests combined, and whales help it flourish. Yet 300,000 whales die in fishing gear every year. 

If you want to read more about WDC, you can do so here: https://whales.org/ 

Keep up to date with all the awesome gaming activities WDC does by signing up to their mailing list here: https://games.whales.org/#newsletter 

And you can find many other amazing games in the sale here: https://bit.ly/WODSale25  
Thank you for joining us and for supporting WDC!

notes.title: SILT - Patch Notes - 1.0.1
notes.notes:
Hi everyone, just a quick update on the new patch we've released today. The patch includes:

[b]NEW FEATURES[/b]

[list]
[*] Added screen-mode option to graphics settings menu. Allows full-screen exclusive or full-screen windowed modes.
[/list]

[b]BUG FIX[/b]

[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where the diver taking damage at the same moment they exit a level could cause the game to hang. 
[*] Fixed a bug that caused unexpected behaviour when the diver died while holding the possession button.
[/list]

[b]SPOILER FIXES[/b]

[b]Gameplay & Balancing Improvements[/b]
[list]
[*] Removed one of the [spoiler]three bobbit worms in Chapter 4, Scene 2 (Bobbit Tunnels 1)[/spoiler]. This makes the puzzle solution more straightforward to execute once the player has figured it out, giving the player more room to [spoiler]safely manoeuvre creatures through that area[/spoiler].
[*] Removed and repositioned some of [spoiler]the jellyfish mines in Chapter 4, Scene 4 (Chasm)[/spoiler]. This makes the traversal of this room slightly more forgiving and less frustrating.
[*] Prevented a soft-lock that could occur in Chapter 4, Scene 7 [spoiler](Nursery 2)[/spoiler] where the player could [spoiler]be trapped in the bottom area of the plant nursery when the light tentacle is damaged[/spoiler].
[/list]
[b]
Quality-of-life [/b]
[list]
[*] Tweaked possession behaviour so that it never targets the creature the player is currently in control of. This helps in situations where the player is trying to possess in a tight space, such as [spoiler]the elevator switches in chapter 3[/spoiler], and should reduce frustrating “mis-possessions”.
[/list]

Thanks for your feedback!

notes.title: Underwater side-scroller Silt could learn a lot from Rain World
notes.notes: There are a few moments from Playdead’s Inside that will live rent-free in my head forever, but my favourite involves a submarine. After you steal the underwater vessel from some unwitting researchers, you crash through a barricade, revealing an entire sunken realm of sky rises, office blocks, and yes, a creepy water troll that tries to drown you and I still shudder to think of. But it did get me thinking about the potential of setting a gloomy side-scroller underwater. Enter Silt... Read more.

notes.title: Silt review: there are plenty of fish in the sea but they're all trying to kill you
notes.notes:
Has anyone coined the term Limbolike yet? 2D side-scrolling platformers that are a bit Tim Burton-y, and possibly in monochrome. Y'know the ones? Silt is a Limbolike, only it's Limbo under the sea. Other free-wheeling associations I have made include Minute Of Islands and, most weirdly, Gormenghast. But having mentioned the later, and because people who like Gormenghast really bloody like Gormenghast (a reasonable position), and respond to its evocation like Chekhov's dogs let loose at the eleventh annual Ringing World National Youth Championship competition, I'm now going to have to temper expectations back down.

Read more

notes.title: 5 Tips for Surviving SILT, Out Tomorrow!
notes.notes:
We’re really excited to finally say that SILT is diving onto Steam tomorrow, and we can’t wait for you to experience the underwater void. To help you as you begin your journey into the harrowing world of SILT, here’s a few hints on how to safely proceed through the abyss. 

[h2][b]Stay in the light - if you can...[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723371/5fff6222cd967fabd401f8feb9f7d611d6b24c29.gif[/img]
Darkness surrounds you in SILT, so you never know what’s waiting for you up ahead. Keep your torch switched on and use the glow of the organisms around you to keep an eye on what’s lurking in the waters...

[h2][b]Use the environment to your advantage[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723371/9700b41bcae36d406fc78b2a364100dd37609cd9.gif[/img]
While it’s a good to assume the worst of the living things that occupy the waters, some might be able to lend a helping hand. For example, some plants you can use to solve puzzles, and a variety of critters can be possessed. See what you can interact with, but always have an escape route planned…

[h2][b]Expect the unexpected[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723371/a73d45072005e2187d1dbab03fdf51136c34d058.gif[/img]
SILT is full of surprises, and not everything is as it seems. This ocean is like no other, so be prepared for some strange encounters.

[h2][b]Get to know the creatures[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723371/09a7fddf989e09f12c54fa085924a76b6b817e7a.gif[/img]
Different creatures have different abilities, and these will help you progress throughout the game. Some friendlier than others, these marine menaces can get you out of some tricky situations.

[h2][b]Approach Goliaths with caution[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723371/10e5ce9b57f5b769266ba8c9604c32bdb7e4b3b4.gif[/img]
This hint is probably self-explanatory. If you see giant jaws, it’s best to keep your distance.

SILT is launching tomorrow, so grab your diving suit and get ready to explore the waters! To keep up to date with the latest SILT news, you can follow us on Twitter [url=https://twitter.com/SiltGame][b]@SiltGame[/b][/url], TikTok [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@silt_game][b]@Silt_Game[/b][/url], or Instagram [url=https://www.instagram.com/spiralcircusgames/][b]@spiralcircusgames[/b][/url].

notes.title: The inspiration behind Silt
notes.notes:
Bizarre creatures, surreal surroundings, and a mysterious oceanic void… All elements that create a harrowing underwater adventure. But how did Silt come to be? Our 2D horror puzzler has been inspired by phobias, games, and even Beatrix Potter. Keep scrolling to find out more!

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/AshGjxTv4J567sBGD0/giphy.gif[/img]

[b]Fear of the deep[/b] 

If you’ve ever experienced [b]thalassophobia[/b], there’s a chance you may find Silt’s oceanic abyss mildly terrifying. Our game artist, Tom Mead, channelled his fear of open water and deep underwater spaces to create an eerie and unnerving environment for the diver to explore. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723371/2601fe6639c397e01d05e4c634b393c21e0132ff.png[/img]

[b]Brilliant indie adventure titles [/b]

Notable games such as [b]Limbo[/b], [b]Inside[/b], [b]Little Nightmares[/b], and [b]Samorost 3[/b] played a big part in inspiring the Spiral Circus team to bring Tom’s artwork to life. These unique and atmospheric visuals reflect the creepy narratives of these games perfectly, which has influenced the creation of Silt from the very beginning. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723371/da903b02be45e91ea3addaf3a2aaac74d1c7baeb.png[/img]

[b]Beatrix Potter[/b]

This may sound obscure, but the main influence of Tom’s art style is in fact [b]Beatrix Potter[/b]. From being scarred as a child watching the animals dressed as humans prancing around, this fuelled the idea for many of Tom’s characters over the years. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40723371/523e6c0d280c177177d51386252cc22bbcf9069f.png[/img]

[b]Can you survive the void?[/b]

Silt is coming to Steam early 2022. To keep up to date with the latest announcements, and to find out more about the origin story of Silt,[url=https://twitter.com/GamesCircus] [b]follow Spiral Circus on Twitter here[/b][/url]. A peculiar adventure soon awaits...

[b]4:30 PM - 5:30 PM | EGX Theatre

notes.title: Dive into a surreal underwater world in Silt, coming early 2022
notes.notes:
[b]Dive into a surreal underwater world in Silt, coming early 2022
[/b]
Hello everyone! Here at Spiral Circus we are excited to finally tell you more about Silt, our surreal underwater exploration game coming to Steam early next year. We just revealed our first trailer at the PC Gaming Show earlier today, so if you haven’t yet seen it, here it is...

[previewyoutube=vdp3whyg3ks;full][/previewyoutube]

Silt is an underwater exploration game set in the depths of an oceanic void, where you play as a diver searching the deep to uncover long-forgotten mysteries. As you explore the depths you’ll encounter deep sea goliaths and use the diver’s ability to possess sea creatures, helping you solve environmental puzzles and dive deeper on your journey. Playing into our own fears of the deep to create a harrowing sense of atmosphere and dread has been key to us while developing Silt, and we hope you get a sense of the mood we’re aiming for from the trailer.

[img]https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/1325890/ss_03f47944158e55389cbc5af094dde6b58fca48c6.600x338.jpg?t=1623622726[/img]

We’re also excited to announce that we’ve partnered with Sold Out as the publisher for the game, and we’ll be sharing much more on Twitter as we get closer to launch, so follow us over at [url=https://twitter.com/gamescircus]@GamesCircus[/url] to keep up with what we’re up to.

And we know it goes without saying, but if you’d like to keep Silt on your radar, please [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1325890/Silt/]add the game to your Wishlist[/url] - it really does help us.

Thanks for your support! See you soon :) Spiral Circus.
